name: MetaClaw

overview_markdown:
MetaClaw is a Python-based meta-learning layer for OpenClaw-style agents: you talk to your agent and it learns and evolves skills from every conversation, with no GPU cluster required. It offers three modes — skills-only, RL (via Tinker), and a default auto mode combining skill evolution with scheduled RL training — plus a 'Contexture' memory layer that persists cross-session user and project facts and injects them into prompts.

Architecturally it ships as a CLI (`metaclaw setup` / `metaclaw start`), an async API server and proxy, and an OpenClaw memory sidecar plugin with endpoints like `/buffer_turn` and `/flush_session` for incremental per-turn memory ingestion (added in v0.4.1). Recent commits show heavy investment in a benchmark suite (metaclaw-bench), Windows cross-platform fixes, and configurable context windows, indicating active, engineering-driven development.

Unlike OpenClaw, which is the canonical personal-assistant runtime, MetaClaw positions itself as a learning/evolution companion rather than a replacement — its value is continual self-improvement and memory, while sandboxing, hardening, and ecosystem breadth remain OpenClaw's strengths.
